title: Functoriality of the associated sheaf on Proj
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be an $\mathbf N$-graded commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj], $S_+=\bigoplus_{n>0}S_n$, and $M,N,L$ be $\mathbf Z$-graded $S$-modules. Write $\widetilde M,\widetilde N,\widetilde L$ for their associated sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (1), whose sections on $D_+(f)$ for homogeneous $f$ of positive degree are $M_{(f)},N_{(f)},L_{(f)}$. For every degree-preserving $S$-linear map $\phi:M\to N$ there is a unique morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\widetilde\phi:\widetilde M\to\widetilde N$ whose map on each such $D_+(f)$ is $x/f^m\mapsto\phi(x)/f^m$. For degree-preserving $\psi:N\to L$, $\widetilde{\psi\circ\phi}=\widetilde\psi\circ\widetilde\phi$, and $\widetilde{\mathrm{id}_M}=\mathrm{id}_{\widetilde M}$. If $\mathfrak p$ is a homogeneous prime of $S$ not containing $S_+$ and $x\in X$ is its point, then under the stalk identifications $(\widetilde M)_x=M_{(\mathfrak p)}$ and $(\widetilde N)_x=N_{(\mathfrak p)}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (c), the stalk map $(\widetilde\phi)_x$ is $y/h\mapsto\phi(y)/h$ for homogeneous $h\notin\mathfrak p$ and homogeneous $y$ with $\deg y=\deg h$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma Tag 01M7 (label lemma-proj-sheaves), final paragraph ('functorial in the graded S-module M'), with the construction preceding Definition Tag 01M6 (label definition-structure-sheaf)

proof.text: For every homogeneous f of positive degree, use the identifications in [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (b) to define a map on standard-open sections by $\widetilde\phi_{D_+(f)}(x/f^m)=\phi(x)/f^m$. The fraction formula is well defined and additive, and it is $S_{(f)}$-linear because $\phi$ is degree-preserving and S-linear; this is the same localization calculation as the fraction maps and semilinearity in [lem-weil-pbc-graded-module-away-restriction] (i).

source.place: Constructions, Lemma Tag 01M7 (label lemma-proj-sheaves), (1)-(3), final paragraph on functoriality in the graded module

proof.text: If D_+(g) is contained in D_+(f), choose a homogeneous relation $g^e=af$. Restricting the formula of Step 1 along $D_+(f)\supseteq D_+(g)$ gives $\phi(a^mx)/g^{em}=a^m\phi(x)/g^{em}$, so the maps commute with the restriction maps $\rho_{f,g}$. The identity and composition laws follow pointwise from [lem-weil-pbc-graded-module-away-restriction] (ii), and the same calculation gives $\widetilde{\psi\circ\phi}=\widetilde\psi\circ\widetilde\phi$ and $\widetilde{\mathrm{id}_M}=\mathrm{id}_{\widetilde M}$ on every standard open.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma Tag 01M4 (label lemma-standard-open), (1)(c),(g),(h), and Lemma Tag 01M7 (label lemma-proj-sheaves), functoriality paragraph

proof.text: The standard opens form a basis with finite refinement by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion]. The maps of Step 1 are compatible with restrictions by Step 2. Apply the basis extension statement [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-of-modules-from-basis] (b) to the two sheaves supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (b): it gives a unique morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\widetilde\phi$ inducing the prescribed maps on all $D_+(f)$.

source.place: Constructions, text before Definition Tag 01M6 and Lemma Tag 01M7 (label lemma-proj-sheaves), final paragraph ('functorial in the graded S-module M')

proof.text: Let x correspond to a homogeneous prime $\mathfrak p$. Under the stalk identifications in [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (c), a germ represented by $y/h$ with h homogeneous and $h\notin\mathfrak p$ is represented on a standard open by the section $y/h$. By the defining formula of Step 1, its image is represented by $\phi(y)/h$. Therefore $(\widetilde\phi)_x(y/h)=\phi(y)/h$.

lean.note: The three modules are indexed by Fin 3. Associated sheaves and their canonical chart/stalk identifications are the data of gradedModuleSheaf_exists, expressed as injective additive maps into the ordinary localizations with prescribed image, scalar law, restriction formula, and germ formula. The conclusion uniquely characterizes induced maps on charts and gives composition, identity, and the stalk fraction formula.
